newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banamex 12-mos net falls 33 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Banamex 12-mos net falls 33 pct on year.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival (Banacci) said on Friday that its banking subsidiary Banco Nacional de Mexico (Banamex) reported a net profit of 1.452 billion pesos for the year 1996.
This was 33 percent lower than the 2.154 billion pesos reported in 1995, it said.
It said that the 12-month operating profit of Banacci fell 18 percent to 2.270 billion pesos, compared to 2.757 billion reported in 1995.
Banamex's capitalization ratio was about 13.1 percent at theend of the year, compared to a previously reported ratio of 14.9 percent at the end of September.
The group said that with the new official accounting rules that apply to Mexican banks this year, it had decided to estimate what its bad loan portfolio will be as of March this year.

"In this way, the amount estimated for the bad loan portfolio for March 1997 under the new rules, 21.316 billion pesos, is 100 percent higher than those officialy reported in December 1996 applying the rules then in effect, 10.624 billion pesos," it said.
It said the net profits of Banamex, excluding the results of its subsidiaries, were 939 million pesos in 1996, down 52 percent from 1.936 billion pesos in 1995.

At the end of 1996, Banamex had reserves against bad loans of 12.931 billion pesos, equal to 61 percent of the bad loan portfolio estimated at March 1997 under the new accounting rules, which establish a minimum reserve level of 45 percent.

Banacci said that in December it completed its capitalization program for Banamex for 8.54 billion pesos as obliged in December 1995, which permitted the sale of 15.0 billion pesos of net portfolio reserves to Fobaproa.
Banacci said it will increase its capital in Banamex by 4.0 billion pesos in 1997, following a December 1996 sale of part of its mortgage portfolio to Fobaproa for a net 8.0 billion pesos.
